newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH DUTY-FREE GRAINS IMPORT TO END FEB 15.
newsitem.headline: POLISH DUTY-FREE GRAINS IMPORT TO END FEB 15.

text.p: The Polish government will publish its decision reinstating customs duty on most grains on Wednesday, which will put an end to their free imports on February 15.

"The resolution of the council of ministers changing the regulation concerning the suspension of collecting duties for certain products will be published on February 5," the government said in a statement.
The government resolutions take effect when they are published in the official government bulletin. The decision on grains imports carries a 10-day grace period.
The duty on the grains, which will not apply to durum wheat, soybeans and maize, will amount to 10 percent, half of the tariff effective until last April.
The duty was suspended to help curb the growth of domestic food prices, which threatened the government's inflation goals last year.
The suspension was scheduled to last until the end of June 1997, but last month Agricuture Minister Roman Jagielinski pushed through the government an early end of duty-free grains imports.

Grzegorz Kolodko, who quit the post of the finance minister on Tuesday, has warned the duty may undermine the government's plans to cut inflation to 13 percent this year from last year's 18.5 percent and openly criticised the cabinet decision.
